CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.prune_umami_events(p_older_than_days integer, p_limit integer DEFAULT 20000)
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'umami', 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_cutoff   timestamptz;
  v_events   integer;
  v_sessions integer;
begin
  -- Floor guard. The delete is irreversible and umami is the only record of
  -- site traffic we keep, so a fat-fingered small value must not be able to
  -- erase the working set. 30 is below any window we would deliberately choose.
  if p_older_than_days is null or p_older_than_days < 30 then
    raise exception 'p_older_than_days must be >= 30 (got %) — this delete cannot be undone',
      p_older_than_days;
  end if;
  if p_limit is null or p_limit < 1 or p_limit > 200000 then
    raise exception 'p_limit must be between 1 and 200000, got %', p_limit;
  end if;

  v_cutoff := now() - make_interval(days => p_older_than_days);

  -- umami.event_data has an FK to website_event ON DELETE CASCADE, so custom
  -- event payloads go with their event and need no separate pass.
  with victims as (
    select event_id
      from umami.website_event
     where created_at < v_cutoff
     order by created_at
     limit p_limit
  )
  delete from umami.website_event e
   using victims v
   where e.event_id = v.event_id;
  get diagnostics v_events = row_count;

  -- Sessions second, and only ones with no events left. A session row is ~470
  -- bytes against an event's ~270, so leaving them behind would make the
  -- session table the larger residue. Bounded by the same p_limit: an
  -- unbounded anti-join over 400k sessions is a seq scan per run.
  with orphans as (
    select s.session_id
      from umami.session s
     where s.created_at < v_cutoff
       and not exists (
         select 1 from umami.website_event e where e.session_id = s.session_id
       )
     order by s.created_at
     limit p_limit
  )
  delete from umami.session s
   using orphans o
   where s.session_id = o.session_id;
  get diagnostics v_sessions = row_count;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'ok', true,
    'cutoff', v_cutoff,
    'events_deleted', v_events,
    'sessions_deleted', v_sessions,
    -- Reported so a run that hit the cap is distinguishable from a run that
    -- finished the backlog. A capped run means the next one still has work.
    'capped', v_events >= p_limit
  );
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.refresh_admin_counts()
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_payload jsonb;
  v_t0 timestamptz := clock_timestamp();
begin
  -- TRY, not blocking. pg_cron does not serialise across jobs, and a queued
  -- worker turns a stall into a pile-up; a skipped tick is free because the
  -- next one recomputes from scratch anyway (the admin_automation_tracking
  -- precedent).
  if not pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('admin_counts_refresh')) then
    return jsonb_build_object('ok', true, 'skipped', 'another refresh holds the lock');
  end if;

  v_payload := public.admin_counts_compute();

  insert into public.admin_counts_cache (id, payload, computed_at)
  values (true, v_payload, now())
  on conflict (id) do update
    set payload = excluded.payload, computed_at = excluded.computed_at;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'ok', true,
    'keys', (select count(*) from jsonb_object_keys(v_payload)),
    'elapsed_ms', round(extract(epoch from (clock_timestamp()-v_t0))*1000));
end
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.refresh_admin_review_queue_counts()
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_union text;
  v_rows  integer;
  v_t0    timestamptz := clock_timestamp();
begin
  -- Only one refresh at a time. pg_cron does not serialise its own jobs, and
  -- this one does a full-corpus scan: two overlapping runs would double the
  -- load this migration exists to remove and then fight over the same 41 rows.
  -- TRY, not blocking -- a skipped tick is free, a queued pg_cron worker turns
  -- a stall into a pile-up (the admin_automation_tracking precedent).
  if not pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('admin_review_queue_counts')) then
    return jsonb_build_object('ok', true, 'skipped', 'another refresh holds the lock');
  end if;

  -- THE SHAPE HERE IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE OBVIOUS ONE IS MEASURABLY WORSE.
  -- This is get_admin_review_summary's own pre-cache query, moved behind a
  -- cron: ONE union, ONE hash join to admin_review_finding_codes, group by.
  --
  -- The first draft instead asked each view for its own counts with
  -- `count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from admin_review_finding_codes
  -- ...))`. That is an aggregate FILTER expression, so it cannot be planned as
  -- a semi-join -- it becomes a correlated subplan evaluated per row, 324k
  -- times, and it does the codes join 41 times instead of once. Measured: it
  -- did not finish inside 60s, against roughly ten for this shape. It is the
  -- same "narrow per-branch count aggregate" that measured 8.03s -- WORSE than
  -- the unpatched function -- while I was choosing between candidate fixes,
  -- and I rebuilt it here without recognising it. Do not re-derive it.
  --
  -- Reusing the old query verbatim also makes the correctness argument short:
  -- the cached numbers are not a reimplementation of the counts, they ARE the
  -- counts, computed by the same expressions over the same views.
  select string_agg(
    format(
      'select u.queue_type,u.subtitle,u.created_at,'
      'coalesce(u.risk_flags->>''risk'',%L)::text risk,%L::integer sla_hours'
      ' from public.%I u',
      r.risk, r.sla_hours, r.view_name),
    ' union all ' order by r.queue_key)
  into v_union
  from public.admin_review_sources r
  where r.active;

  if v_union is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('ok', false, 'reason', 'no active review sources');
  end if;

  -- Driven FROM admin_review_sources with a LEFT JOIN, so a source with zero
  -- items still gets a row of zeros. `group by queue_type` alone emits nothing
  -- for an empty source, which would leave the cache incomplete and make
  -- "every active source has a cached row" unassertable -- the reader
  -- coalesces anyway, but a complete cache is the difference between a
  -- sentinel that can see a missing source and one that cannot.
  execute format($q$
    with authorized as (
      select u.*,
        sla_hours is not null and u.created_at < now()-make_interval(hours=>sla_hours) as overdue,
        (f.queue_key is not null) as is_finding
      from (%s) u
      left join public.admin_review_finding_codes f
        on f.queue_key=u.queue_type and f.subtitle_match=u.subtitle),
    agg as (
      select queue_type, count(*) n, count(*) filter(where overdue) late,
        count(*) filter(where is_finding) findings,
        count(*) filter(where not is_finding) decisions,
        count(*) filter(where risk='safety') safety
      from authorized group by queue_type),
    fresh as (
      select r.queue_key, coalesce(a.n,0) n, coalesce(a.late,0) late,
        coalesce(a.findings,0) findings, coalesce(a.decisions,0) decisions,
        coalesce(a.safety,0) safety
      from public.admin_review_sources r
      left join agg a on a.queue_type = r.queue_key
      where r.active)
    insert into public.admin_review_queue_counts
      (queue_key, n, late, findings, decisions, safety, computed_at)
    select queue_key, n, late, findings, decisions, safety, now() from fresh
    on conflict (queue_key) do update
      set n = excluded.n, late = excluded.late, findings = excluded.findings,
          decisions = excluded.decisions, safety = excluded.safety,
          computed_at = excluded.computed_at
  $q$, v_union);
  get diagnostics v_rows = row_count;

  delete from public.admin_review_queue_counts c
  where not exists (
    select 1 from public.admin_review_sources r
    where r.active and r.queue_key = c.queue_key);

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'ok', true,
    'sources', v_rows,
    'elapsed_ms', round(extract(epoch from clock_timestamp() - v_t0) * 1000));
end
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.refresh_admin_review_queue_top()
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public', 'pg_temp'
AS $function$
declare
  v_union text;
  v_rows  integer;
  v_depth integer := public.admin_review_queue_top_depth();
  v_t0    timestamptz := clock_timestamp();
begin
  if not pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('admin_review_queue_top')) then
    return jsonb_build_object('ok', true, 'skipped', 'another refresh holds the lock');
  end if;

  select string_agg(format(
    'select u.id,u.queue_type,u.content_type,u.title,u.subtitle,u.created_at,u.confidence_score,'
    ' case u.risk_flags->>''severity'' when ''critical'' then 4 when ''high'' then 3'
    ' else case coalesce(u.risk_flags->>''risk'',%L) when ''safety'' then 2'
    ' when ''integrity'' then 1 else 0 end end urgency_rank,'
    ' %L::text source_label,coalesce(u.risk_flags->>''risk'',%L)::text risk,'
    ' %L::boolean public_impact,%L::integer sla_hours,%L::integer priority_weight,'
    ' %L::boolean can_reopen from public.%I u',
    r.risk, r.label, r.risk, r.public_impact, r.sla_hours, r.priority_weight,
    r.can_reopen, r.view_name), ' union all ' order by r.queue_key)
  into v_union
  from public.admin_review_sources r
  where r.active;

  if v_union is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('ok', false, 'reason', 'no active review sources');
  end if;

  delete from public.admin_review_queue_top;

  -- ONE union execution, fifteen bounded top-N sorts over the materialized result. The obvious
  -- shape -- one statement per (scope,sort) -- re-executes the union fifteen times; a single pass
  -- is ~950ms warm, so that alone would be a 14s tick. `as materialized` is load-bearing: the CTE
  -- is referenced from inside a LATERAL that runs once per combination, and without the hint
  -- Postgres is free to inline it and re-plan the union fifteen times, which is the same defect
  -- wearing a CTE's clothes.
  --
  -- The scope and sort expressions are transcribed from get_admin_review_queue. P6 asserts the
  -- resulting order matches the live path by executing both and comparing, rather than trusting
  -- the transcription -- a copied ORDER BY that drifts is invisible to every structural check.
  execute format($q$
    insert into public.admin_review_queue_top
      (scope, sort, rank, queue_type, id, urgency_rank, source_label, risk,
       public_impact, sla_hours, priority_weight, can_reopen, is_finding, created_at, computed_at)
    with authorized as materialized (
      select a.*,
        a.sla_hours is not null and a.created_at < now()-make_interval(hours=>a.sla_hours) as overdue,
        (f.queue_key is not null) as is_finding
      from (%s) a
      left join public.admin_review_finding_codes f
        on f.queue_key = a.queue_type and f.subtitle_match = a.subtitle)
    select s.scope, o.sort, r.rank, r.queue_type, r.id, r.urgency_rank, r.source_label, r.risk,
           r.public_impact, r.sla_hours, r.priority_weight, r.can_reopen, r.is_finding,
           r.created_at, now()
    from (values ('all'),('safety'),('overdue'),('public'),('decisions')) s(scope)
    cross join (values ('priority'),('age'),('confidence')) o(sort)
    cross join lateral (
      -- THE LIMIT MUST APPLY BEFORE row_number(), AND THE OBVIOUS SHAPE GETS THIS WRONG.
      -- A window function sorts its whole partition and no LIMIT can be pushed through it, so
      -- `row_number() over (order by ...) ... limit 250` in ONE level is fifteen full sorts of
      -- 335k rows. Measured on prod: 20,640 ms. Ranking the already-bounded 250-row subquery
      -- instead makes each pass a bounded top-N: 5,871 ms, a 3.5x difference from nesting alone.
      select sub.*, row_number() over (
        order by
          case when o.sort='priority' then sub.urgency_rank else 0 end desc,
          case when o.sort='priority' then sub.overdue else false end desc,
          case when o.sort='priority' then sub.priority_weight else 0 end desc,
          case when o.sort='confidence' then sub.confidence_score end asc nulls last,
          sub.created_at asc nulls last, sub.queue_type, sub.id) as rank
      from (
        select t.* from authorized t
        where case s.scope
                when 'all'     then true
                when 'safety'  then t.risk = 'safety'
                when 'public'  then t.public_impact
                when 'overdue' then t.overdue
                else                not t.is_finding
              end
        order by
          case when o.sort='priority' then t.urgency_rank else 0 end desc,
          case when o.sort='priority' then t.overdue else false end desc,
          case when o.sort='priority' then t.priority_weight else 0 end desc,
          case when o.sort='confidence' then t.confidence_score end asc nulls last,
          t.created_at asc nulls last, t.queue_type, t.id
        limit %s
      ) sub
    ) r
  $q$, v_union, v_depth);
  get diagnostics v_rows = row_count;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'ok', true,
    'rows', v_rows,
    'depth', v_depth,
    'elapsed_ms', round(extract(epoch from clock_timestamp() - v_t0) * 1000));
end
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.run_staging_reconcile_committed(p_batch integer DEFAULT 2000)
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
DECLARE
  v_committed int := 0;
  v_rejected  int := 0;
BEGIN
  -- At */5 a slow pass can still be running when the next one fires. TRY, never
  -- block: a skipped tick is free (the work is idempotent and the next tick is
  -- 5 minutes away), whereas a queued pg_cron worker turns one slow run into a
  -- pile-up — the failure that deadlocked the projector and the reaper.
  IF NOT pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('staging_reconcile_committed')) THEN
    RETURN jsonb_build_object('skipped', 'another run holds the lock');
  END IF;

  -- Class A: the pipeline committed it and the target row still exists.
  WITH cand AS (
    SELECT s.id
      FROM public.ingestion_staging s
     WHERE s.review_status = 'pending_review'
       AND s.target_record_id IS NOT NULL
       -- Re-resolve the pointer per target table. A dangling uuid is not proof.
       AND (
            (s.target_table = 'news_articles'        AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.news_articles        x WHERE x.id = s.target_record_id))
         OR (s.target_table = 'venues'               AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.venues               x WHERE x.id = s.target_record_id))
         OR (s.target_table = 'marketplace_listings' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.marketplace_listings x WHERE x.id = s.target_record_id))
         OR (s.target_table = 'events'               AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.events               x WHERE x.id = s.target_record_id))
         OR (s.target_table = 'personalities'        AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.personalities        x WHERE x.id = s.target_record_id))
         OR (s.target_table = 'cities'               AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.cities               x WHERE x.id = s.target_record_id))
         OR (s.target_table = 'countries'            AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.countries            x WHERE x.id = s.target_record_id))
       )
     ORDER BY s.created_at
     LIMIT p_batch
  )
  UPDATE public.ingestion_staging s
     SET review_status = 'auto',
         disposition   = 'committed',
         reviewed_by   = NULL,
         reviewed_at   = now(),
         review_notes  = left(
           'auto-reconcile: already committed to ' || s.target_table ||
           ' (' || s.target_record_id::text || '); review_status was stale'
           || CASE WHEN s.review_notes IS NULL OR length(trim(s.review_notes)) = 0
                   THEN '' ELSE ' | ' || s.review_notes END, 2000)
    FROM cand
   WHERE s.id = cand.id;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_committed = ROW_COUNT;

  -- Class B: the pipeline already rejected it; only the status lagged.
  WITH cand AS (
    SELECT s.id
      FROM public.ingestion_staging s
     WHERE s.review_status = 'pending_review'
       AND s.target_record_id IS NULL
       AND s.disposition = 'rejected'
     ORDER BY s.created_at
     LIMIT p_batch
  )
  UPDATE public.ingestion_staging s
     SET review_status = 'rejected',
         reviewed_by   = NULL,
         reviewed_at   = now(),
         review_notes  = left(
           'auto-reconcile: pipeline already rejected this row; review_status was stale'
           || CASE WHEN s.review_notes IS NULL OR length(trim(s.review_notes)) = 0
                   THEN '' ELSE ' | ' || s.review_notes END, 2000)
    FROM cand
   WHERE s.id = cand.id;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rejected = ROW_COUNT;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'reconciled_committed', v_committed,
    'reconciled_rejected',  v_rejected,
    'still_pending', (SELECT count(*) FROM public.ingestion_staging WHERE review_status = 'pending_review')
  );
END
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.admin_counts_compute()
 RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  result jsonb; estimates jsonb; v_sla jsonb := '{}'::jsonb;
  v_cnt bigint; v_overdue bigint; r record;
  sla_feedback_h constant int := 48;
  sla_event_quality_h constant int := 336;
begin
  select jsonb_object_agg(relname,reltuples::bigint) into estimates
  from pg_class where relnamespace='public'::regnamespace and relname=any(array[
    'venues','events','news_articles','personalities','cities','countries','hotels',
    'queer_villages','marketplace_listings','community_groups','unified_tags',
    'cms_pages','email_ingestions','workflow_runs','scrape_sources','content_links',
    'community_submissions','redirects']);
  result := coalesce(estimates,'{}'::jsonb);
  for r in select queue_key,view_name,count_key,count_prefix,sla_hours
           from triage_sources where active order by queue_key loop
    execute format(
      'select count(*),count(*) filter(where created_at < now() - %L::interval) from public.%I',
      r.sla_hours || ' hours',r.view_name) into v_cnt,v_overdue;
    result := result || jsonb_build_object(r.count_prefix||r.count_key,v_cnt)
      || jsonb_build_object(r.count_prefix||r.count_key||'_overdue',v_overdue);
    v_sla := v_sla || jsonb_build_object(r.count_key,r.sla_hours);
  end loop;
  result := result || jsonb_build_object(
    'review_feedback',(select count(*) from community_submissions
      where content_type='feedback' and feedback_status in ('new','under_review')),
    'review_feedback_overdue',(select count(*) from community_submissions
      where content_type='feedback' and feedback_status in ('new','under_review')
        and submitted_at < now()-(sla_feedback_h||' hours')::interval),
    'review_group_requests',(select count(*) from group_join_requests where status='pending'),
    'quality_existence',(select count(*) from entity_existence_audit
      where action='flag' and reverted_at is null),
    'quality_glossary',coalesce((select total_count from public.tag_editorial_queue(1,0,null) limit 1),0),
    'quality_personality',(select count(*) from public.triage_src_quality_personality),
    'quality_event',(select count(*) from public.event_quality_issues where status='open'),
    'quality_event_overdue',(select count(*) from public.event_quality_issues
      where status='open' and severity in ('critical','high')
        and detected_at<now()-(sla_event_quality_h||' hours')::interval),
    'sla_hours',v_sla||jsonb_build_object('feedback',sla_feedback_h,
      'quality_event',sla_event_quality_h)
  );
  return result;
end
$function$

user_events_retention.rationale: Exact age cutoff with >=30-day floor and bounded deletion. No semantic judgment; keep retention in code. No retention policy changes authorized by this audit.

umami_retention.rationale: Exact timestamp retention and orphan-session cleanup, bounded with a 30-day minimum. No need to send visitor/session data to a model.

admin_counts_refresh.rationale: Writes aggregate dashboard cache only. Existing database count/view predicates remain code; a model must not invent counts or certify underlying records.

admin_review_counts_refresh.rationale: Registry-driven count/SLA aggregation into a cache. Reads source-view decisions without changing them. Preserve exact counts and deterministic deadlines.

admin_review_queue_top_refresh.rationale: Cache of code-defined scope, ordering and bounded ranks, not a factual approval. Registry views supply evidence upstream; no model judgment belongs in cache refresh.

existence_signals_purge.rationale: Retains newest 20 signals per entity and removes older-than-180-day surplus. No entity closure or factual inference. Unbounded statement timeout/loop remains an operational review item.

staging_rejected_purge.rationale: Existing rejected disposition plus age>90 days selects retention deletion. No new rejection judgment. Keep evidence-retention policy in code; audit/event preservation is a separate requirement.

review_queue_retention.rationale: Existing status, age and staging referential state drive retention. Jev should not decide expiry. The existing age>90-day predicate also deletes pending rows and merits a separate retention-policy review; this audit does not approve that behavior.

marketplace_ownership_apply.rationale: Copies ownership tags only from approved canonical brand registry matches. Never replace explicit approval with model identity/ownership inference. Registry authorization and brand matching remain separate trust dependencies.

staging_reconcile_committed.rationale: Target-row existence reconciles lifecycle metadata without changing canonical content, but can close stale review on legacy wrongly admitted rows. Preserve classification corrections separately; do not count reconciliation as factual verification.

marketplace_review_autotriage.rationale: Automatically applies proposed subcategory when regex/rating gate permits. It does not verify that proposed taxonomy is actually correct. Needs an evaluated typed taxonomy judgment at the native apply boundary, preserving adult-content protections.

marketplace_relevance_rescore_weekly.rationale: Legacy audience-fit scoring directly changes canonical scores. Version73 adds strict parsing, snapshot guards and accurate counters, but Jev adoption needs a separate audience-fit evaluation; explicit LGBTQ-topic scores are not interchangeable with adult scene/brand audience fit.

marketplace_catalog_prune.rationale: Live native functions inspected separately: explicit domain allowlist, recent classified_at, score<0.6, featured/brand/wishlist exclusions. Currently completed/disabled with no active cron. Preserve disabled state; a score alone is not new validated publication authority.
